correctness.rationale: Every seven-vertex orientation has a unique 21-bit code. A score-pruned binary decision tree exhausts all regular codes, and a directed-triangle bit rule enumerates every legal move. Independently, three catalogue seed orientations generate all 2640 states under S7 relabelling and use outgoing-neighbor-mask moves. Both executable methods agree on 18480 edges, three complete BFS profiles, converse distances and 30 exact-cover Fano planes. The seven-step converse/Fano equivalence is proved combinatorially, not inferred from experiments; BFS is exhaustive for the finite domain. The numerical checks were rerun using the actual packaged scripts.

originality.rationale: The full 2000 McShine primary paper and a later complete published interchange-graph discussion were read; known connectivity, degree, and the Brualdi–Li diameter conjecture are excluded from the contribution. The new finite claim is the three complete labelled seven-tournament distance profiles, the converse-geodesic Fano classification, and the unique 360 unordered antipodal pairs. These statements are not contained in inspected material, and none follows from the published general connectivity or conjectured diameter alone. Important residual risk: full 1984 original chapter unavailable, so this is best-knowledge originality rather than proven historical priority.
residual_risks: The directly relevant Brualdi–Li (1984) book chapter was not fully accessible and may already contain the seven-vertex distance and converse results.
Unindexed historical papers or tables using triangle switches rather than interchange terminology might contain equivalent calculations.
This self-review originality judgement is provisional and is not a guarantee of independent scholarly priority.

value.rationale: The classical regular-tournament interchange graph is a natural finite benchmark for fixed-score sampling and its long-standing diameter prediction. The exact 2640-state metric and 360 converse antipodes refine the predicted diameter sharply, while the Fano-plane decomposition equivalence explains which tournaments admit the shortest possible converse transformations. A meaningful structural obstruction and full finite graph census are obtained without claiming an all-orders theorem.
